title: A nonlinear theory for chemotactic fronts of mixed populations
summary: Collective migration of heterogeneous cell populations is central to many biological and physiological processes, including development and immune response. Recent experimental and theoretical advances have shown how asymmetric interactions with self-generated chemical gradients shape the spatial distribution of distinct cell types within migrating collectives. However, the principles governing robust spatial organisation of heterogeneous cell populations remain poorly understood.
